description: Scripted byte-stream lifecycle scenarios. Each step feeds one event to a fresh transport and expects the exact step Core answers with. Timer ids are allocated 1, 2, ... per transport and never reused; write ids likewise. Platform adapters reuse these scenarios to prove they execute the effects Core returns.

scenarios.name: frames queued during discovery flush once connected, then a clean EOF terminates with 0
discovery that never finds an endpoint times out once
a connect that never completes times out on its own budget, not the discovery remainder
a connect failure reports the host message and terminates with 1
a port above 65535 from the provider fails before any connect
port zero from the provider fails before any connect
a negative port from the provider fails before any connect
an empty host from the provider fails before any connect
an endpoint reported twice or for a stale generation is ignored
a cancelled startup timer that fires anyway cannot fail a ready stream
a stalled write times out and terminates with 1
custom limits shape the armed deadlines
only one write is in flight and frames go out in order
exceeding the queued frame count fails the stream and refuses further sends
exceeding the queued byte budget fails the stream, but filling it exactly is allowed
completed writes free their share of the byte budget
a completed write makes room for the next frame
a user stop is silent and invalidates every outstanding callback
a stopped transport can start again and ignores the previous run's callbacks
starting twice keeps the running lifecycle
finishing a stream with queued frames drains them silently once the last write completes
the drain deadline closes a stream whose peer stopped reading, without a termination
a failure while draining stays silent
a write timeout while draining stays silent
finishing with nothing queued, or before the stream is ready, closes immediately
finishing a ready stream with an empty queue closes immediately
starting while a drain is pending replaces it and ignores the old drain's callbacks
events for a stream that never started are ignored or refused
